name: experiment-preflight
description: Mandatory check before any results-bearing run (training, ablation, benchmark, evaluation sweep, pilot or calibration run) that the experiment measures what it claims. Builds a frozen packet, gets the reviews its tier requires (light: one fresh reviewer; full: fresh Claude + fresh Codex with blind reconstruction), and gates the start on them passing. Use before starting such a run, when writing a spec/prereg, when asked for a "preflight", or when reviewing an experiment packet.
---

# Experiment pre-flight

Implements the Experiments section of the global AGENTS.md. A repository procedure that
covers the same steps (e.g. a custody or prereg workflow) may replace the mechanics; it may
not drop a step without an explicit user decision. Invocation, exchange and recording of
reviews: skill `peer`.

## Roles
Author builds the packet. Coordinator dispatches reviewers and records verdicts. Full tier: two
reviewers, one fresh Claude session, one fresh Codex session. Light tier: one fresh reviewer.
The author is never a reviewer.

## Stages
- **Deterministic check with a known answer:** a test (asserted prediction, fails with the
  mechanism removed), not a packet.
- **Technical test** (it runs, shapes, no NaN, no crash; outputs not looked at as results):
  no pre-flight needed, results are not evidence.
- **Pilot / calibration packet:** anything whose outputs inform a decision, including smoke
  runs whose numbers are read, data statistics used for predictions, and instrument
  calibration. Reviewed prospectively: it states controls, expected signatures, budget and
  stop conditions, but need not supply the evidence it is meant to produce. Its results stay
  labelled as pilot exposure.
- **Confirmation packet:** requires the pilot's measurement checks to have passed. When the
  pilot only feeds thresholds that can be stated relatively (paired seeds, effect larger than a
  within-run repeat), pilot and confirmation are one packet and one review cycle.

## Tiers
- **Light:** no decision rests on the run, it is not a confirmation run, and it is either a
  short pilot or calibration (total budget over all cells and seeds within the limit the
  repository sets; without one, it is not short) or runs on synthetic data with a known ground
  truth. One file `packet.md`: the user's questions verbatim, gates with null probes, exact
  command, run plan, stop condition. One fresh reviewer, one round: alignment with the
  questions, what the command measures, applicable checklist items; then a delta answer on
  revisions. Commit the packet, then record outside it the commit hash and `sha256(packet.md)`:
  together they are the digest.
- **Full:** everything else, and whenever in doubt: both layers, manifest, two reviewers,
  procedure below.

## The packet (full tier)
Two layers, stored where the repository keeps specs/evidence (otherwise
`preflight/<run-id>/` next to the spec):

- **Layer A — intent-free** (`layer-a.md`): baseline and candidate commits with the diff,
  resolved config per cell, exact commands, run plan (cells, seeds, budget, stop conditions),
  data identifiers, paths of evaluation/metric code. No question, hypothesis or expectation.
- **Layer B — intent** (`layer-b.md`): opens with the user's questions verbatim (numbered)
  and, if the repository has a goal file, the goal item served and why this run is the shortest
  path to it; then question, hypothesis, prediction, what an ineffective
  method would show, kill condition, decision rule, controls, replication unit and size,
  smallest decision-relevant effect, analysis (metrics with units, summaries, selection rules).
- **Manifest** (`manifest.txt`): the content of everything the run reads, file by file, never
  through `git diff` (external diff and textconv drivers can change or empty its output). From
  the repository root:
  ```
  python3 <this skill>/manifest.py --exclude <packet dir> --exclude <run-output dirs or files> \
    <ignored inputs: data, configs, env files> <packet dir>/layer-a.md <packet dir>/layer-b.md \
    > <packet dir>/manifest.txt
  ```
  Tracked, submodule and untracked non-ignored files are included automatically, except under
  `--exclude`, which takes directories or files (so verdicts, logs, outputs of earlier cells and
  a status file updated at start do not change the digest).
  Untracked files inside submodules are not collected: pass any the run reads as extras. Record
  the exact manifest command in Layer A; the start gate reruns it unchanged. A large
  dataset may be passed as a file holding its immutable version id instead.
  Commit everything first, including the packet and any status file: the manifest records the
  commit, so a later commit changes the digest.
  **Packet digest = sha256 of `manifest.txt`.** Reviews and logs live outside the manifest. For
  the diff shown to reviewers use `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv`.
  Self-check: `bash <this skill>/test_manifest.sh`.

## Reviewer procedure (full tier)
Round 1 gets Layer A plus repository access and states the rule: do not open specs, preregs or
result logs before round 2. (This is instruction-only; the reviewer could read them. Record it.)

1. **Reconstruct, from Layer A only:** what does each cell measure, in which units; what result
   would a no-op method produce; which degenerate solution would score well; what can this run
   not distinguish.
2. **Round 2 gets Layer B.** First judge whether the run serves the user's questions at all, and
   confirm or contradict the goal item and its shortest-path claim; then **compare** the
   reconstruction with the intent. Any mismatch is a blocker.
3. **Checklist** below plus every entry of the repository's LESSONS file: evidence, or `n/a`
   with a reason.
4. **Verdict:** `PASS | REVISE | BLOCK`, packet digest, reconstruction, mismatches, checklist
   results, blocking vs. optional findings.

## Checklist
Items marked † (5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 17, 19, 23) need evidence that a pilot or calibration run may be meant to produce. In a pilot
packet they are reviewed as a plan (what is measured, expected signature, stop condition); a
confirmation packet needs them passed.

**Question ↔ configuration**
1. The config is derived for this question; anything inherited from an earlier run is justified.
2. Every weight, threshold and tolerance has a unit and a reference scale checked against our
   data; numbers copied from papers or examples are converted; combined terms are compared in
   magnitude at initialization.
3. Borrowed terms are read from the implementation, not the paper: quantity, normalization,
   schedule, gradient paths, and whether an advertised feature actually fires.
4. If two scales or conditions coincide in all test cases, one case separates them.
5. † Predictions on new data follow a measurement of that data's own statistics.
6. Raw data and actual input/target examples were looked at, from the start and the end of each
   source.

**Mechanism** (each: if applicable)
7. † A deterministic check on a case with known answer shows the term does what the derivation
   says: values and gradients.
8. † Information flows, not only gradients: swapping or removing a source changes the output;
   changing hidden or future content leaves it unchanged.
9. † Teacher before student: an estimate used as a target beats the quantity it replaces.
10. The target is derivable from the input, and no shortcut lets the answer be read off an input.
11. Every path or case that should work is actually produced by the sampler.

**False successes**
12. Degenerate solutions (collapse, clones, shrink, wrong-but-consistent) are named and either
    excluded or caught by a hard gate. Collapse is measured scale-invariantly on the quantity
    that should carry information; no penalty can be bypassed by rescaling.
13. Ablations actually remove the information they claim to remove.
14. † A missing or deferred measurement is never a pass; it blocks.

**Measurement validity**
15. Metrics cannot be gamed: fixed units, coverage and signed values beside unsigned distances,
    subsets reported with counts, measured where targets differ rather than averaged away.
16. † Positive and negative controls show that the evaluation as a whole rejects the relevant
    false successes, not just that one mechanism works.
17. † Replication unit, justified number of replications, uncertainty analysis and the smallest
    decision-relevant effect are stated; the plan can separate that effect from noise.

**Comparison design**
18. Arms differ only in the variable under test: a switch does not shift random streams; equal
    seeds give equal weights, batches and evaluation data.
19. † Budgets are matched and long enough that the base task is learned in every arm.
20. Tuning and evaluation data are separate, and training cannot reach the evaluation set.
21. Selection rules (time point, aggregation, thresholds) are fixed before results are seen.
22. Randomized parameters are tested for their actual distribution, not only valid shapes.

**Execution**
23. † The real code path runs end to end with the final configuration (technical test, or a
    pilot packet if outputs are read).
24. Budget, guards and stop rules per stage, enforced in code; timeout means unevaluated, not
    failed; peak memory measured at the largest configuration.
25. Runtime or speed-up predictions follow a profile of the baseline and a cost model.
26. Shared devices: the repository's resource limits per device are respected; outputs are
    merged, never overwritten.

## Start gate
- Start only with the tier's `PASS` verdicts (light: one, full: two) on the same packet digest.
- Before **every** start, check the concrete cell against the run plan and the digest against
  the reviewed one. Light tier: the tree is clean at the recorded commit and `sha256(packet.md)`
  matches. Full tier: rebuild the manifest from the live state. Use the repository's runner if
  it does this, otherwise the coordinator does and records it.
- Any change outside the frozen run plan needs new reviews. No blanket approval for adaptive
  search.

## After the run
- Audit as a referee from raw outputs: recompute summaries, check units and controls.
- A changed analysis is a new, labelled exploratory version; the original analysis and raw data
  stay. Negative and failed runs are kept.
- An unexpected scientific outcome does not by itself stop or invalidate the remaining run plan.
  Document every surprise, its evidence and its effect on interpretation in the report, and
  continue the authorized plan. Enforced resource and technical validity limits still apply;
  any change to the plan or analysis must be explicit and versioned.
- Every avoidable loss becomes a lesson with its safeguard at the repository's canonical place.

The recovery procedure needs a durable timeout record; I won’t treat the clarification as already implemented.

Shared collapse, the partial sampled oracle, inherited Auto/fallback asymmetry, and two same-host repeats are explicit limitations—not unresolved demands for a broader experiment. The supplied clarifications preserve the frozen scope except for the timeout recovery procedure described below.

Two issues prevent an unqualified FULL preflight pass:

1. **Timeout recovery can produce a success verdict.** Outer `timeout` can terminate Python after all eleven result files exist, before `failure.json` is written. There is no SIGTERM handler. A subsequent `diagnose.py report` then evaluates complete rows and can display “pilot passed” without an incomplete-execution warning. This contradicts the frozen total-timeout rule. [Failure handling](/home/alex/Documents/IntrinsicEngine/tasks/evidence/METHOD-078/diagnose.py:228), [report status](/home/alex/Documents/IntrinsicEngine/tasks/evidence/METHOD-078/diagnose.py:113)

Verify the specific case **all result files present + timeout**. Merely rerunning `report` is insufficient. This needs a packet revision and new digest; it is not automatically covered by the current clarification.

I excluded it from reasoning, but cannot certify an unexposed reconstruction.
